Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Household, washing & chores

comb noun and verb

also comb your hair, comb out, comb back

classical

Traupman 36, 38, 164
Traupman 293

pecten, pectinis m.

noun, third declension

Other words

  • pectō, pectere

    verb, third conjugation · classical · Ov. H. 13.39: comam pectere (Lewis & Short s.v. coma); Traupman 36, 38, 164; Traupman 293

  • repectō, repectere, —, repexum — comb back, comb again

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Ov. AA 3.154: coma repexa (Lewis & Short); Traupman 38: to comb back, repectere; Traupman 167; Traupman 293

    (vōx poētica: Ov., Stat.)

  • expectere — comb out

    also used · modern · Traupman 38: to comb out, expectere; Traupman 167; Traupman 293

    Traupman’s compound; not in Lewis & Short.

  • prōpexus, prōpexa, prōpexum — combed forward

    declension · also used · classical · Lewis & Short s.v. prōpexus; Traupman 167: prōpectere, to comb forward

    (vōx poētica (Lewis & Short))

    Only the participle is found; Traupman makes a verb of it.

Examples

  • Pectinem mihi dā.

    Give me the comb.composed

  • Capillōs pecte.

    Comb your hair.composed

  • capillōs (crīnēs, comam) pectere

    to comb one’s hairTraupman 38

  • capillum (capillōs, crīnēs, comam) pectere

    to comb the hairTraupman 293

See also hair.
